pue_new_hyperscale.source: LBNL 2024 US Data Center Energy Usage Report (Shehabi et al.) â€” fleet 1.4 in 2023, 1.15-1.35 projected 2028; hyperscale and colo already under 1.4
pue_new_hyperscale.note: Ohio is ASHRAE zone 5A (mixed-humid). Lei & Masanet's zone-specific values exist only in their Figures 4-5 and are not extractable from the text; a citing paper reports ~1.32 for mixed-humid. Treat 1.32 as a second-hand upper anchor.

load_factor.source: Muller, NBER w35100 (2026-04) â€” load = net utilized kW x PUE x 8760 x load factor
load_factor.note:
CONFLICT TO RESOLVE: the AEP Schedule DCT tariff requires an 85% minimum
demand charge, which looks like a utilization floor. It is not the same
quantity. The tariff's 85% is a BILLING floor on subscribed capacity;
this 0.55 is energy against DESIGN IT capacity. Pick one to drive
facility_mwh and record which, or you will double-count.
(Moot for Wilmington anyway â€” AES Ohio, not AEP.)

retail_rate_delta_residential_iou.source: Meeks et al. 2026, investor-owned utilities subsample
retail_rate_delta_residential_iou.note: USE THIS ONE for Wilmington. AES Ohio is an IOU.

retail_rate_delta_residential_all.source: Meeks et al. 2026, residential class, pooled
retail_rate_delta_residential_all.note: Commonly MISLABELLED as the all-customer average. The all-customer figure is 0.027. Label carefully.

retail_rate_delta_residential_public.source: Meeks et al. 2026 â€” reported as 'smaller' than IOU, no point estimate extracted

retail_rate_delta_residential_coop.source: Meeks et al. 2026 â€” no measurable effect for cooperatives

aes_dct_minimum_demand_pct.source: AES Ohio tariff exhibit, 2026-09-03 â€” minimum billing demand is 85% of Contract Capacity, including during ramp

aes_dct_service_term_years.source: AES Ohio tariff exhibit â€” minimum 10-year term following ramp completion

aes_dct_mw_threshold.source: AES Ohio tariff exhibit â€” aggregate monthly maximum demand > 25,000 kW at a single location

aes_dct_ramp_years.source: AES Ohio tariff exhibit â€” maximum 2 years to reach full contract capacity
aes_dct_ramp_years.note:
CONFLICT WITH THE PJM DATA. Dayton-2025-002 shows a 2028-2030 ramp
(35 -> 100 -> 300 -> 500 MW), which is ~2.75 years from first energization.
Either the tariff clock starts at facilities-complete rather than first
service, or the PJM need covers more than one customer. Flag in output.

aes_dct_network_upgrade_cost_share_custo.source: AES Ohio tariff exhibit â€” customer pays actual costs of transmission network upgrades and supplemental transmission projects the company would not have planned absent the request
aes_dct_network_upgrade_cost_share_custo.note:
** THE MOST IMPORTANT NUMBER IN THE RATEPAYER MODULE. **
If this holds, the $589.8M of committed Clinton-area transmission work
does NOT land on ratepayers, and the Meeks +5.2% IOU estimate becomes an
UPPER BOUND rather than a central case â€” most utilities in that 2010-2024
sample had no such tariff.
Two caveats before relying on it:
  1. It covers TRANSMISSION. Distribution-level work on the 69 kV system
     may still be socialised.
  2. A minimum-take protects against stranded cost; it does not guarantee
     zero rate impact.
Model BOTH arms: tariff-as-written vs tariff-rejected.

residual_bill_share_under_tariff.source: OUR ASSUMPTION. No published estimate exists for how much of the Meeks IOU rate effect survives a tariff that assigns 100% of transmission network upgrade cost to the customer.
residual_bill_share_under_tariff.note:
What this represents: the tariff covers TRANSMISSION. Distribution-level
work on the 69 kV system, general system effects, and anything AES would
have built anyway are NOT assigned to the customer and still reach
ratepayers. The band is deliberately wide because we are guessing.
EXPECT THIS TO BE A TOP TORNADO DRIVER. That is correct and useful â€”
it says this is the number worth researching next.

aes_dct_exit_fee_basis.source: AES Ohio tariff exhibit â€” 36 months notice, plus the HIGHER of (a) minimum charge for at least 75% of the service term or (b) actual facility costs x fraction of term remaining

aes_dct_mandatory.source: AES Ohio tariff exhibit â€” service 'is required' for customers meeting the data center definition and size thresholds
aes_dct_mandatory.note: Mandatory, not elective. AWS cannot opt out into a general service tariff.

household_bill_delta_iou.source: Meeks et al. 2026, authors' own translation at pre-treatment prices and sales

water_l_per_kwh_evaporative.source: Microsoft Americas WUE 0.34 (FY25) / 0.38 (FY24); LBNL 2024 site WUE ~0.36; hyperscale median 0.32. Upper bound 1.1 derived from Google's Aug 2025 per-prompt figures â€” OUR arithmetic, not disclosed by Google.

water_l_per_kwh_closed_loop.note: Traded against a 10-35% energy penalty. The spread between cooling types is one of the largest single levers in the model.

water_indirect_l_per_kwh.source: LBNL 2024 â€” indirect (power generation) water intensity; US average 4.35
water_indirect_l_per_kwh.note:
ROUGHLY 12x THE DIRECT FIGURE. The water impact of a data center is
overwhelmingly at the generating stations, not at the facility. This
lands on the upstream spine and it reframes the whole water narrative.
Caveat: includes reservoir evaporation and is contested.

aws_wilmington_claimed_water.source: Clinton County Port Authority â€” A PARTY TO THE PROJECT. Claims 97% outside-air cooling.
aws_wilmington_claimed_water.note:
THIS IS THE SINGLE BIGGEST UNVERIFIED SENSITIVITY IN THE MODEL.
It sits 25-40x BELOW LBNL-derived norms (~1,350-2,280 gal/day/MW).
Plausible for a genuinely air-cooled Ohio design, but it is a developer
claim, not a finding. Show it WITH its uncertainty band and provenance.

marginal_co2_lb_per_mwh.source: EPA eGRID2023rev2, RFCW subregion, NON-BASELOAD rate (2025-06-12)
marginal_co2_lb_per_mwh.note: The average rate is 911.4. Use non-baseload â€” new data center load is marginal load. Using the average understates by ~47%. EPA AVERT would be the upgrade if time allows.

capex_construction_share.source: Virginia JLARC Report 598 (independent legislative audit, 2024-12) â€” 19.6% building and site, 68.2% equipment
capex_construction_share.note:
ONLY ~20% OF HEADLINE CAPEX IS CONSTRUCTION.
AWS's $4B in Wilmington is roughly $800M of actual construction.
Multiplying headline capex by a jobs-per-dollar coefficient inflates
the answer ~5x and is the most common error in this literature.

construction_jobs_per_musd_construction.source: Georgia Dept of Audits / UGA Carl Vinson (2025-12), multiplier 1.79. JLARC parallel: 4.45 direct, 7.49 total, multiplier 1.68.

construction_duration_months_per_buildin.source: JLARC 598 p.14; AWS New Carlisle IN Phase 1 observed Sept 2024 - Dec 2025
construction_duration_months_per_buildin.note: 5+ years per campus. The binding constraint is TRANSFORMERS AND GRID INTERCONNECTION, not civil works â€” model delay on the power side.

permanent_jobs_per_mw.source: JLARC 598; AWS New Carlisle bottom-up (6-9 staff/shift per 65MW building); Meta Bowling Green OH (~100 jobs per 200-250MW)
permanent_jobs_per_mw.note:
At 500 MW this gives ~200 permanent. The Port Authority claims 100+,
which cross-validates at ~0.25/MW (our low bound).
DO NOT USE colocation figures (0.87-1.6/MW) â€” wrong facility type.

operations_multiplier.note: NOT the industry's 6.6-7.5. See the do-not-use list below.

self_reported_headcount_haircut.source: JLARC 598 halved operator-reported employment because operators count contractors as jobs
self_reported_headcount_haircut.note: Apply to EVERY self-reported headcount, including the Port Authority's.

population_response_to_jobs.source: DERIVED FROM THE DHL NATURAL EXPERIMENT, Clinton County 2007-2024: job base fell 43-49% while population fell 2.0%.
population_response_to_jobs.note:
This directly contradicts the standard economic-impact assumption that
jobs drive population. In THIS county they demonstrably do not â€”
adjustment runs through labor-force participation and out-commuting.
Reinforced by the commute shed: 62.9% of county jobs are already held
by in-commuters from 320 counties.

acres_per_mw.source: NO PRIMARY SOURCE EXISTS. Consultant consensus 0.5-1.5 ac/MW. Comparables: Stargate Abilene ~1,100 ac / 1.2 GW (~0.9); Meta Hyperion 3,650 ac.
acres_per_mw.note:
BETTER OPTION AVAILABLE: derive this from the actual Wilmington parcel.
471.609 acres against a 500 MW PJM ramp = 0.943 ac/MW, from county
records rather than a vendor blog. Use the local value and cite it.

ohio_assessment_ratio.source: Ohio statutory assessment ratio â€” assessed value is 35% of market value

school_state_aid_floor.source: ORC 3317.017 â€” state share floored at 10% of base cost once local capacity / base cost > 0.90
school_state_aid_floor.note: 105 of 611 Ohio districts are ALREADY at this floor. Wilmington is at 18.395%, with only $679.74/pupil of headroom.

land_value_premium_pct_per_100mw.source: OUR ASSUMPTION. No published estimate for Ohio. Directionally supported by reporting on land speculation around announced campuses.

cash_rent_passthrough.source: OUR ASSUMPTION â€” share of a land value change that reaches cash rent within the horizon.
cash_rent_passthrough.note: Clinton cash rent is $170/ac against Ohio's $188, so margins are already thin and pass-through may bind harder than average.

farm_exit_rate_per_rent_pct.unit: fraction of farms per 1% rent rise

backlash_index_per_usd_bill.source: OUR ASSUMPTION, but the MECHANISM is documented: PUCO 25-0958-EL-AIR drew hundreds of ratepayer comments plus formal opposition resolutions from Logan, Greene and Champaign county commissioners and five municipalities.

moratorium_threshold.source: OUR ASSUMPTION â€” backlash index at which further expansion is blocked.
moratorium_threshold.note: Grounded precedent: data centers were on the ballot in 18 Ohio communities in Nov 2026, and Clinton County commissioners denied a 715-acre rezoning 3-0.

sanitary_gal_per_mw_day.source: OUR ASSUMPTION. Data centers have few occupants; sanitary load is small, but cooling blowdown reaches the sewer where cooling is not fully air-cooled.
sanitary_gal_per_mw_day.note: Matters because Wilmington's WWTP runs at 2.97 of 3.0 MGD design â€” 99% of capacity.

chiller_sound_power_dba.source: OUR ASSUMPTION from typical industrial chiller ratings. Runs continuously.

generator_sound_power_dba.source: OUR ASSUMPTION. Real Ohio EPA PTI filings show 115 generators at Lima and up to 158 at Amazon Hilliard, so the COUNT is grounded even where the level is not.

ground_attenuation_db.source: ISO 9613-2 ground effect over soft ground

marginal_heat_rate_btu_per_kwh.source: Combined-cycle gas at the efficient end, simple-cycle peakers at the inefficient end. PJM marginal units are predominantly gas.

utica_well_lifetime_mcf.source: Utica horizontal well estimated ultimate recovery, typical range 2-8 Bcf
utica_well_lifetime_mcf.note: Used for a well-equivalent figure, NOT a claim that specific wells were drilled for this facility.

backlash_decay_per_year.source: OUR ASSUMPTION. Political salience decays between election cycles.
backlash_decay_per_year.note:
Without decay the backlash index is an unbounded cumulative sum and a
moratorium fires in ~92% of draws, which tells you nothing. With decay
the index reaches a steady state of (bill * gain / decay), so the loop
becomes DISCRIMINATING: it fires when bills rise enough to sustain
opposition, not merely because time passed.

construction_wage_usd_per_year.source: BLS OES Ohio construction trades, loaded for overtime on a large industrial build. PLACEHOLDER RANGE â€” needs a specific OES series cite before it goes on a slide.
construction_wage_usd_per_year.note: Previously hardcoded as 85000 in the engine, which violated the rule that numbers live here with a source.

school_share_of_property_tax.source: Typical Ohio school district share of total effective property tax millage. NEEDS the Clinton County Auditor's millage breakdown for Wilmington CSD before it goes on a slide.
school_share_of_property_tax.note:
Without this channel the model saw only the state-aid LOSS from
un-abated value and none of the local tax GAIN, so it concluded 100%
abatement was optimal for schools. That is backwards by roughly $9M/yr.

air_cooled_pue_penalty.source: Microsoft, 2024-12-09 â€” zero-water cooling traded against higher energy. Already noted on water_l_per_kwh_closed_loop; this is the coefficient that finally applies it.
air_cooled_pue_penalty.note: Makes cooling a real trade-off: water against energy and CO2. Before this it changed water only.

bill_reference_mw.source: Meeks et al. estimate a per-FACILITY rate effect for 'a large data center'. We anchor that to a 500 MW reference so the effect scales with absolute size rather than with fraction-of-contract, which was 1.0 at full build for any contract.

mwh_per_home.source: EIA average US residential electricity consumption, ~10,500 kWh/yr

water_rate_passthrough_pct_per_pct_capac.unit: % residential rate rise per % of system capacity consumed
water_rate_passthrough_pct_per_pct_capac.source: OUR ASSUMPTION, carried over from the frontend's placeholder engine. A real figure needs Wilmington's water rate study.
